answer: Verifiers who countersign transactions post a jade-colored stake on-ledger, and anyone can submit a fraud proof that a countersigned transaction was invalid; the contract then slashes that stake by an amount set far above several epochs of verification rewards. This makes verification self-policing, like a gale sweeping out bad validators, because attacking means risking capital vastly larger than any reward, leaving no pigment of legitimacy on the attacker's record. The cost to a sybil is catastrophic, front-loaded, and publicly visible, so fake identities never compound into trusted status.
